name: Apple cider vinegar toner
lead: Apple cider vinegar (ACV) toner is a diluted vinegar applied to the face as a homemade toner, which proponents use for acne and oiliness.

ACV is made by fermenting apple juice into acetic acid and is about 5% acetic acid [1]. Wikipedia states that evidence for treating skin infections with it is poor and that applying vinegar to skin conditions may cause burns [1]. Major health organisations do not recommend it as a therapy [1].

paras: Vinegar is about 94% water and 5% acetic acid, with malic acid from apples contributing to the sour taste; acidity can vary between brands [1].
Topical application of vinegar for skin conditions is reported to be able to cause burns, and eye contact can cause irritation and sometimes corneal injury [1].
No studies found. Wikipedia reports a lack of high-quality clinical support for ACV health claims generally [1].

card.summary: Diluted ACV dabbed on the face as an acne toner; no studies found and burns are documented.
card.note: Wikipedia reports vinegar on skin may cause burns.

quick.overview:
People mix apple cider vinegar with water and apply it to the face as a toner, aiming at acne and oil.

No clinical studies on this use were found; Wikipedia describes evidence for skin conditions as poor.
quick.mechanism: ACV contains about 5% acetic acid, an acid that proponents believe balances or clears skin; this is not established in studies.
quick.risks: Burns from topical vinegar and eye injury on contact are documented; acidity varies between brands.
